section.name: Apache Tomcat 11.x vulnerabilities
section.p: This page lists all security vulnerabilities fixed in released versions of Apache Tomcat® 11.x.
Note: Vulnerabilities that are not Tomcat vulnerabilities but have either been incorrectly reported against Tomcat or where Tomcat provides a workaround are listed at the end of this page.

section.name: Fixed in Apache Tomcat 11.0.25

p.strong: Low: DoS in WebSocket chat example

section.p: The WebSocket chat example provided an unbounded buffer for undelivered messages.

Affects: 11.0.0-M20 to 11.0.24
Users who followed the security guidance to remove the examples web application are not affected.

section.name: Fixed in Apache Tomcat 11.0.21

p.strong: Note: The issue below was fixed in Apache Tomcat 11.0.20 but the release vote for the 11.0.20 release candidate did not pass.
Important: The fix for CVE-2026-29146 allowed the bypass of the EncryptInterceptor

section.p: An error in the fix for CVE-2026-29146 allowed the EncryptInterceptor to be bypassed.
This was fixed in revision 1840057 and reported as bug 69420.
Important: Remote Code Execution via session persistence CVE-2026-11111, CVE-2026-22222

ul.li: an attacker is able to control the contents of a file; and
the server is configured to use the PersistenceManager

section.p: then remote code execution is possible. See the announcement.
section.o: Applications that do not use non-blocking I/O are not exposed to this vulnerability.

section.name: Fixed in Apache Tomcat 11.0.12

p.strong: Moderate: Multiple weaknesses in HTTP DIGEST authentication

section.p: An entry whose header carries no severity rating.

section.name: Not a vulnerability in Tomcat

p.strong: Critical: Remote Code Execution via log4j

section.p: Apache Tomcat does not ship with log4j. This is not a vulnerability in Apache Tomcat.
